```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3, out.width = "100%")
library(excalidrawer)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Stickers

Twelve community libraries from <https://libraries.excalidraw.com> come with
the package. Stickers are native Excalidraw elements: hand-drawn, editable,
and recolourable.

```{r}
table(exc_stickers()$library)
```

```{r, fig.height = 4}
exc_sticker_sheet("stick-figures", columns = 5) |> plot()
```

```{r}
exc_scene(exc_text("Sticker party", 0, 0, font_size = 36)) |>
  exc_sticker("stick-figures:Girl", 0, 60, width = 90) |>
  exc_sticker("r-icons:1", 120, 70, width = 90) |>
  exc_sticker("bubbles:1", 230, 50, width = 160) |>
  exc_sticker("stars:3", 420, 70, width = 70, stroke = "#f08c00", fill = "#ffec99",
              fill_style = "solid") |>
  plot()
```

Any other library works too: `exc_library("https://...excalidrawlib")` and
`exc_library_item()`.

## Hand-drawn people

`exc_peep()` draws people in Pablo Stanley's Open Peeps style. Each seed is a
different person; see `exc_peep_options()` for faces, heads and accessories.

```{r}
exc_scene() |>
  exc_peep(0, 0, seed = "Ada", face = "smile") |>
  exc_peep(170, 0, seed = "Grace", clothing = "#a5d8ff") |>
  exc_peep(340, 0, seed = "Hadley", face = "cheeky") |>
  plot()
```

## Templates

Design a card or poster in Excalidraw, with `{{column}}` in its text, and
shapes labelled `{{chart:name}}` or `{{image:name}}` where charts and images
should go. Then fill it from data:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
card <- exc_template_fill(
  exc_template_example(),
  data = list(metric = "Sketches drawn", value = "1,204", change = "+18% this month"),
  charts = list(trend = ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:12, y = c(3, 4, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 11, 10, 12)),
                               aes(x, y)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#1971c2") +
                  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_excalidraw(base_size = 11))
)
plot(card)
```

`exc_template_render()` does this for every row of a data frame and saves one
file per row.

## Diagrams

`exc_mermaid()` converts Mermaid text into editable Excalidraw shapes with
Excalidraw's own converter (it needs Chrome, through the chromote package).
`exc_d2()` renders D2 diagrams in D2's sketch mode, if the `d2` program is
installed.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
exc_mermaid("flowchart LR\n  A[Data] --> B[Sketch it] --> C[Share]") |> plot()
exc_d2("data -> sketch -> share") |> plot()
```

## More fonts

```{r}
exc_fonts()
```

`exc_font_fetch("xkcd")` downloads the xkcd Script font (non-commercial
licence) for `font = "xkcd Script"`.

## Sketch Studio

`run_sketch_studio()` puts all of this behind a point-and-click app, around
the live Excalidraw editor.
